title: Two competing incidents — question explanation
learningObjective: Prioritize incidents by impact, exposure, time sensitivity and containment needs
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: An organization has two alerts: (A) malware is actively encrypting files on a shared operational server; (B) a single employee received a suspicious email but did not open it. Both require triage.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Prioritize incidents by impact, exposure, time sensitivity and containment needs
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option D: Prioritize the active encryption event for immediate coordinated containment while ensuring the email is reported and triaged. Active disruption and potential spread represent immediate operational risk; the lower-impact email still needs handling.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Delaying containment during active encryption may increase damage. Option B: General prevalence does not outweigh evidence of active encryption and immediate operational impact. Option C: Incidents differ in impact, scope, active harm and urgency; equal priority is not risk-based.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Activate the incident-response plan, coordinate containment of the actively affected system, assign triage to the email and document priority rationale. Prioritization considers current impact, scope, exposure, time sensitivity and containment opportunity.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Prioritization considers current impact, scope, exposure, time sensitivity and containment opportunity.

Option B is unsafe because General prevalence does not outweigh evidence of active encryption and immediate operational impact. Option C is unsafe because Incidents differ in impact, scope, active harm and urgency; equal priority is not risk-based. In practice: Activate the incident-response plan, coordinate containment of the actively affected system, assign triage to the email and document priority rationale. Key takeaway: Prioritization considers current impact, scope, exposure, time sensitivity and containment opportunity.
